prompt:
Add a `tasklist` extension: a list item whose text starts with `[ ]`, `[x]` or `[X]` followed by a space becomes a task.
- The marker is replaced by `<input type="checkbox">`, `checked` for `x`/`X`, and `disabled` unless the `clickable` option is true (default false).
- The `<li>` gets the class from the `item_class` option (default `task`).
- It works in ordered and unordered lists, nested lists and loose lists, and keeps inline markup after the marker.
Register it so `markdown.Markdown(extensions=['tasklist'])` works once installed.

Work on your own; nobody will answer questions. When you finish, report: status `done` if you did the task, `not_found` if something the task names does not exist, `blocked` if you could not do it; `answer` holds any answer the task asks for (otherwise one short sentence); `changed` lists the files you changed.

report.answer: I added the `tasklist` extension. `markdown.Markdown(extensions=['tasklist'])` now works, and the full test suite passes (1144 tests run, 112 skipped). flake8 isn't installed here, so it was not run. A list item starting with `[ ]`, `[x]` or `[X]` and a space gets a checkbox in place of the marker. The checkbox is `checked` for x/X and `disabled` unless `clickable` is true. The `<li>` gets the `item_class` class (default `task`). This works in ordered, unordered, nested and loose lists, and inline markup after the marker still renders. In a loose list, the checkbox goes at the start of the item's first paragraph. The marker is read before inline parsing, so a reference definition like `[x]: url` won't turn it into a link. If attr_list also adds a class, the output is `class="task extra"`. I added docs, the changelog entry and registration in both `pyproject.toml` and the fixture's entry-points file. The changelog entry has no issue number (`#123`) because there isn't one. I also added "checkbox" and "checkboxes" to the spelling dictionary.

check.why: task lists everywhere, options, entry point, docs, tests and changelog
